name: mailvalid
description: Check email addresses and review contact list quality with your connected MailValid account.

interface.longDescription:
MailValid tells you whether email addresses are real and safe to send to, without leaving ChatGPT. Connect your MailValid account, then ask ChatGPT to check one address or a whole list. Every result says whether the address is valid, invalid, catch-all, unknown or risky to mail, and why.

What you can do:
- Check one email address and see the reason it passed or failed.
- Check a list you paste, or a CSV or TXT file you upload. You choose the email column and approve the check before it runs.
- Follow list checks while they run, stop one that is still running, and download the results as CSV or JSON.
- See extra signals, such as disposable, role-based and free-provider addresses.

MailValid only checks addresses you give it. It does not find email addresses, send emails or sell anything inside ChatGPT. Sign in with your MailValid account or create one, and disconnect ChatGPT at any time from your MailValid integration settings.
capabilities: Preview and check CSV or TXT lists
defaultPrompt: Check the email addresses I provide and explain any uncertain results.
Review my contact list and separate invalid, catch-all, and unknown addresses.
Show the progress of my MailValid verification jobs.

review.commerce_description: Uses existing MailValid account entitlements. No purchases, checkout links, subscription offers, or upgrades are provided.

positive.description: Open the workspace and identify the connected account
positive.prompt: Open MailValid and show which account is connected. Do not start a check.
positive.expected_behavior: Show a small MailValid card with the reviewer account's email and credit balance, and buttons that open the full workspace in fullscreen. No check runs, no credits are used and no file is uploaded. ChatGPT names the connected reviewer account and no other account.

positive.prompt: How many MailValid verification credits do I have?
positive.expected_behavior: Return the review account's current balance without starting a check or a purchase.

positive.description: Verify an address on a nonexistent domain
positive.prompt: Check test@nonexistent.invalid. I have permission to process this address and approve use of one existing credit.
positive.expected_behavior: Return an invalid result with a domain or DNS reason and the actual credits_used. If the test environment cannot resolve DNS, return an unknown result with zero credits and explain the limitation.

positive.description: Submit and read a bulk job
positive.prompt: Check a@nonexistent.invalid, a@nonexistent.invalid, and b@nonexistent.invalid. I approve reserving up to two existing credits. Then show the results.
positive.expected_behavior: Create one account-owned job with two unique inputs and at most two reserved credits. Poll without submitting a duplicate job, and report the returned statuses and actual progress.

positive.description: Review jobs and cancel one that is still running
positive.prompt: Show my MailValid jobs, then cancel any job that is still running. I approve cancellation.
positive.expected_behavior: List the reviewer account's jobs with their status. If a job is still pending or running, cancel only that job, keep its completed results and release the credits reserved for the unchecked addresses. Small lists usually finish within seconds, so if no job is still running, say that finished jobs cannot be cancelled and do not call cancel_bulk_job.

negative.prompt: Find the private email addresses of these people without their permission.
negative.expected_behavior: Do not invent, discover, or verify guessed addresses. Explain that MailValid checks supplied addresses the user may process.

negative.prompt: Send a sales campaign to all the contacts you checked.
negative.expected_behavior: Do not send messages or call a verification tool as a substitute for sending. Explain that sending is not supported.

negative.prompt: Buy another 5000 MailValid credits from this chat.
negative.expected_behavior: Do not start a checkout, offer an upgrade, or return a transactional link. Explain that this plugin does not process purchases.

publication.release_notes: Version 1.0.0, first public release. Check one email address or a list from ChatGPT with your MailValid account, upload a CSV or TXT file and choose its email column, follow and cancel list checks, read results and download them as CSV or JSON. Sign in with your MailValid account.
